short: Albedo is the fraction of incoming light that a surface or body reflects, from 0 (absorbs everything) to 1 (reflects everything).
For an object orbiting the Earth, perigee is the point of closest approach and apogee is the point farthest away.
A short document recording a significant technical decision and why it was made.
The astronomical unit (AU) is a unit of length, defined as exactly 149,597,870,700 metres. It is close to the average distance between the Earth and the Sun.
A black body is an idealised object that absorbs all radiation falling on it and emits radiation whose spectrum depends only on its temperature.
A carbon budget is the total amount of carbon dioxide that can still be emitted while keeping global warming below a chosen limit, with a stated level of likelihood.
The Doppler shift is the change in the observed frequency or wavelength of a wave caused by relative motion between source and observer.
Earth observation is gathering information about the land, oceans and atmosphere, mainly using satellites and other remote sensors.
The greenhouse gas emissions released making and delivering a product or building.
Emissivity is the ratio of the thermal radiation a surface emits to what a perfect black body would emit at the same temperature, between 0 and 1.
A geostationary orbit is a circular orbit about 35,786 km above the equator, in which a satellite takes one sidereal day to circle the Earth.
The greenhouse effect is the warming of a planet's surface caused by atmospheric gases that absorb outgoing thermal radiation and re-emit part of it back towards the surface.
A facility on Earth that communicates with spacecraft.
Light pollution is excessive or misdirected artificial light that brightens the night sky and affects people, wildlife and observation.
The accounting of gains and losses between transmitter and receiver.
Magnitude is a logarithmic scale for the brightness of astronomical objects. A difference of 5 magnitudes corresponds to a brightness ratio of 100.
The server that holds the original version of a site's content.
Remote sensing is acquiring information about an object or area without direct contact, typically by measuring radiation with instruments on satellites, aircraft or drones.
How strong a signal is compared with the background noise.
A spectral line is a narrow feature in a spectrum, appearing as a dark absorption line or bright emission line at a wavelength characteristic of a particular atom or molecule.
Star formation is the process by which dense regions within cold clouds of gas and dust collapse under gravity to form stars.
The transit method detects a planet around another star by measuring the small, periodic dip in the star's brightness when the planet passes in front of it.
